layers.note: A small pencil cholla, often growing up through other shrubs.

moisture.note: Deserts, grasslands and chaparral, on sandy, loamy or gravelly ground.

elevation_m.note: 40 to 1,500 m (Flora of North America); 1,000 to 5,000 feet in southern Arizona (Kearney and Peebles).

shade_tolerance.note: Often within the canopy of mesquite and other shrubs: some shade borne.

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about 3 to 17 °C; gone below 0 °C and above 20 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −15 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −20 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 27 to 33 °C; gone below 25 °C, where summers are too short, and above 35 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 5,500 to 10,000 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 4,500.

degree_days_5.note: About 3,800 to 8,200 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 3,000.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.08 to 0.7, gone by 0.04 and above 0.9.

summer_rain.note: Needs the monsoon's summer rain: from about 0.3 of the year's precipitation in summer, gone below 0.2; up to about 0.75, gone by 0.85.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Saguaro desert scene (the west bajada of Saguaro National Park's Tucson Mountain District, about 750 m, 32.25 N 111.17 W) from general knowledge of the species and the ranges, habitats and elevations in the sources read for its spec (2026-10-19). Christmas cholla grows from Arizona to Oklahoma and Texas and south into northern and central Mexico, in the Sonoran and Chihuahuan deserts and their grasslands (Flora of North America). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records; every full range holds the bajada's climate (coldest month about 11 °C, warmest about 31 °C, about 7,600 degree-days above 0 °C, coldest night about −4 °C, moisture index about 0.15, about half the year's rain in summer).
